clue.text: In Le Monde, Mrs Boatman follows article on cuckoo

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the article right after the first piece
follows puts the setter's pronoun after everything before it

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy, mad
A is the indefinite article
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as ME

explanation.surface: A French newspaper reports the setter's wife responding to an article about a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often stand for ME in their own clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The French form of address for a married woman, equivalent to the English title Mrs.

clue.text: Destined to wander around and around, fed up

indicators.note: the second around wraps the reversed wandering word about the other piece
the first around turns the word for wandering backwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means read the word fed from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fated to drift in circles has had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'around's do different jobs: the first turns a word backwards, the second wraps it round the other piece; 'up' reverses in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut out or intended for something is being destined for it, as in 'they were made for each other'.

clue.text: Several pointless clues for one in the sea

indicators.note: the compass point S (south) is dropped from the word

parts.note: divers is an old word for several, as in 'divers ways'

explanation.surface: A handful of hints that lack any point help someone out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' means without a compass point, here S; 'clues for' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer who goes beneath the waves is someone found in the sea.

clue.text: Troop movement in April?

definitions.meaning: a parade of soldiers filing past a saluting base
by April the month of March is over, already gone by

explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half literally: in April, March has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade of soldiers past a dignitary is a formal military procession.

clue.text: Eat little fish caught here, in an area of the sea

parts.note: to fast is to eat little or nothing
a net is where caught fish end up

explanation.surface: Advice on dieting while fishing in some stretch of ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: FASTNET is a sea area of the British shipping forecast, which is the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastnet is one of the named regions in the BBC shipping forecast, off southern Ireland.

clue.text: Area of sea said to be modest source of fish

indicators.note: said to be signals that the words are heard spoken

parts.note: fair means modest or moderate, and roes are fish eggs, the source of fish

explanation.surface: A stretch of ocean is reportedly a humble supplier of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR ROES spoken sounds like FAEROES, a shipping forecast area north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faeroes is one of the regions named in the shipping forecast, around the islands of that name.

clue.text: Part of sea route is shut off

indicators.note: off says the letters of the phrase are rearranged, as something gone off is spoiled

explanation.surface: A stretch of a shipping lane has been closed.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTH UTSIRE, an area off Norway in the shipping forecast, spans 5 and 29.
explanation.definitionFit: South Utsire is one of the named divisions of the North Sea in the shipping forecast.

clue.text: Regional variation about superior brain support

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the other piece
variation says the letters of Regional are varied, rearranged

parts.note: U is short for upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: Local differences surrounding a better kind of mental backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges REGIONAL, and 'about' puts it round U, the old label for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroglia are the cells that hold up and nourish nerve cells, the supporting tissue of the brain.

clue.text: It goes into the sea with a message inside

indicators.note: inside says the answer sits within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A bottle carrying a note drifts out into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: London's river flows out into the North Sea, and Thames is also a shipping forecast area.

clue.text: As a rib might carry one to get inshore

indicators.note: the answer, if it carried one more letter, would become the word for inshore, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: coastal means near the shore, inshore
A means one, as in a single

explanation.surface: A rib, perhaps a small inflatable boat, ferries someone back to shore.
explanation.walkthrough: A RIB is also a rigid inflatable boat, hence the nautical surface; add A to the answer and you get COASTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Costal is the anatomical adjective for things relating to the ribs.

clue.text: Two areas of the sea in which to find fish

parts.note: Dover is a shipping forecast area in the Channel
Sole is a shipping forecast area southwest of Cornwall

explanation.surface: A pair of ocean regions where fish can be caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish caught in the Channel and prized in restaurants, one species of sole.

clue.text: Uniform visual spread is lacking? It depends on the palate

parts.note: U is uniform in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: spread says the remaining letters are spread about, rearranged
lacking takes away the word is from visual

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A consistent picture is missing, which hinges on one's taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lacking' takes IS from VISUAL, leaving VUAL, which 'spread' rearranges to VULA.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy flap hanging from the soft palate at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Area of sea foam produced with small rotation

indicators.note: a small rotation of two letters, one shifting past its neighbour

parts.note: froth is foam

explanation.surface: Foam churned up in some stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the R and O of FROTH gives FORTH, a shipping forecast area off east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forth is a named region in the shipping forecast, off the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: Overly large number in those mixed with taste

parts.note: too means overly

indicators.note: in puts the large number inside the rearranged letters
mixed says the letters of those are rearranged

parts.note: M, Roman numeral for a thousand, is a large number

explanation.surface: Far too many of those items have been blended with seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges THOSE to THSOE, and 'in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is tasty, so it comes with plenty of flavour.

clue.text: Don't do this to a boat entirely in the sea

parts.words: Don't do this to a boat
parts.note: the idiom 'don't rock the boat'
all means entirely, as in 'all wet'

explanation.surface: A warning to keep a vessel steady while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCKALL is both an islet and a shipping forecast area west of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a shipping forecast region far out in the Atlantic, so it lies out in the ocean.

clue.text: "Worth, perhaps, 1 euro" — curt fashion statement

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are shaped anew

parts.note: 1 looks like I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A designer's clothes price tag reads one euro, a blunt message.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Frederick Worth was a 19th-century Paris dressmaker, the founder of haute couture.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is an example of a fashion house founder, a dress designer of the highest class.

clue.text: Burden of tragic, boring speech

indicators.note: speech signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: sad is tragic and dull is boring

explanation.surface: The load of a sad, tedious oration.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD DULL run together sounds like SADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To saddle someone is to burden them, as with a debt.

clue.text: Good-looking sailor spends night here?

parts.note: a sailor asleep spends the night in a boat of dreams, but the phrase means a handsome person

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a vessel slept on; the real sense is an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a very attractive person, a heartthrob.

clue.text: Rebuke solver twice, say, in sea area report!

indicators.note: twice says the letter is used two times
in places the spoken letters for the solver among the others
report signals the sea area's name heard spoken, as four T's

parts.note: Forties is a shipping forecast area in the North Sea

indicators.note: say signals the word for the solver heard as a letter

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A scolding for the puzzler, delivered in the shipping forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: FORTIES spoken sounds like 'four T's' and 'you' like U: the four T's hold two U's, one in each pair, so it is TUT twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is an exclamation of disapproval, used as a mild reproach.

clue.text: The boat's back! Deliverance! The boat's back!

indicators.note: back means the final letter of the word boat

parts.note: a ransom buys a captive's deliverance

explanation.surface: Joyful cries that a vessel has returned, framing an exclamation of rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase is used twice: once as definition, once for its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is the flat surface forming the stern of a boat.

clue.text: See 22
Fashionable tempo and a voice on one note

parts.note: in means fashionable
T is an abbreviation for tempo in music
a means one

explanation.surface: Stylish timing and a single singer holding one pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant or speak in a monotone.

clue.text: Row over eccentric letters sent out from superior eating place

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts this piece above the next

parts.note: din is a row, a noise

indicators.note: eccentric letters are the off-centre ones at the edges, and they are sent out

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: An argument over strange correspondence dispatched from a high-class restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: BETTER loses its outer letters B and R, leaving ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining area, an alcove for meals.

clue.text: Time to try for scale

parts.note: as means for, in the sense of because
size is scale, extent

explanation.surface: A moment to attempt measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSIZES were the old periodic sittings of English county courts, when cases were tried.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a court session, a period set aside for trying cases.

clue.text: Where swirling sea breaks into coastline? Thud! Crash!

indicators.note: breaks into puts the churned sea inside the other letters
crash says the letters of coastline and thud are smashed up
swirling says the letters of sea are churned round

explanation.surface: Waves pound the shore with a heavy noise and a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHEAST ICELAND, spanning 22 and 19, is a shipping forecast area.
explanation.definitionFit: Southeast Iceland is a named place in the shipping forecast, answering where a ship is.

clue.text: Drummer has one to bash about what's inside

indicators.note: about puts the striking word around the other piece

parts.note: to hit is to bash

indicators.note: inside means the inner letters of the word what

explanation.surface: A percussionist owns something to strike, whatever is in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-hat is a pair of cymbals on a stand worked by a pedal, part of a drum kit.

clue.text: Where liners originally entered the sea?

definitions.text: Where liners originally entered the sea?

indicators.note: entered puts the initial letter into the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of liners

explanation.surface: A question about the place where ocean ships were first launched.
explanation.walkthrough: MALIN is a shipping forecast area off northwest Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Malin is a stretch of sea in the forecast where liners sail, the clue reading as a whole.

clue.text: Sea area, say, for two days off across the Channel

definitions.text: for two days off across the Channel

indicators.note: say signals the forecast area's name heard spoken

parts.note: Lundy is a shipping forecast area in the Bristol Channel

explanation.surface: A forecast region, perhaps, for a weekend break in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Lundi is French for Monday, the day after the two days off at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the first working day of the week, following the weekend, is lundi.

clue.text: Airship loses skin, ending up in middle of sea

indicators.note: the last letter moves up into the middle
loses skin removes the outer letters of airship

explanation.surface: A blimp is damaged and comes down mid-ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRSHIP without its skin is IRSHI; 'ending up in middle' moves the final I into the middle. The Irish Sea is a forecast area.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish as in the Irish Sea, one of the shipping forecast regions.

clue.text: Protective cover for Spooner's style of hairlines?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a bun is a style of hair
a sonnet is a style of lines of verse

explanation.surface: A guard for one's hair lines, credited to the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'hairlines' must be split into hair and lines to find the two pieces Spooner swaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbonnet is a brimmed hat protecting the face and neck from sunlight.

clue.text: It's wrong or right inside: not exactly mature

indicators.note: inside puts the letter for right within the other letters
not exactly says the letters of mature are inexactly arranged

explanation.surface: Something is mistaken, or else correct at heart: a not-quite-grown-up attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, something that is incorrect.

clue.text: See 5
